RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of discrimination. Academic appointments depend heavily on departmental fit, interview performance, and specific curricular needs; the announcement explicitly highlighted the successful candidate's industry background, which economics departments frequently prioritize for applied teaching and student employability.

Raising the panel's gender without documented proof of bias will appear unfounded, likely damage your professional reputation, and undermine any future candidacies. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on your interviews to strengthen future applications. Only consider pursuing a formal inquiry if objective procedural violations or demonstrable bias emerge from institutional records, preferably after consulting a union representative or employment specialist.
